outline: 550 The Derivative of a Linear Function

examples.question_text: The tangent to $y=f(x)$ at $P(4,3)$ passes through $Q(1,9)$. Find $f'(4)$.
examples.solution_text:
The derivative is the gradient of the tangent.
$\begin{align*}f'(4)&=\frac{3-9}{4-1}\\&=\frac{-6}{3}\\&=-2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. Find $f'(3)$ using the labelled points on the tangent.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.65cm,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black}]\definecolor{curveBlue}{HTML}{268CFF}\definecolor{tangentOrange}{HTML}{EF8B2C}\draw[black,->] (0,0)--(6,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[black,->] (0,0)--(0,7) node[above] {$y$};\draw[curveBlue,thick,domain=0.5:5.5,samples=60] plot (\x,{0.4*(\x-3)*(\x-3)+\x-1});\draw[tangentOrange,thick] (1,0)--(6,5);\fill[black] (3,2) circle (2pt);\fill[black] (5,4) circle (2pt);\path (3,2) node[below right] {$P(3,2)$};\path (5,4) node[below right] {$Q(5,4)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
examples.solution_text:
Read the two labelled points on the orange tangent.
$\begin{align*}f'(3)&=\frac{4-2}{5-3}\\&=\frac{2}{2}\\&=1\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A secant joins two distinct points on a curve. A tangent has the same local gradient as the curve at $x=a$. Which line gives the average rate of change, and which gives $f'(a)$?
examples.solution_text: The secant gradient gives the average rate of change between its two points. The tangent gradient gives the instantaneous rate of change at $x=a$, written $f'(a)$.

examples.question_text: A secant joins $P(d,F(d))$ and $Q(d+r,F(d+r))$, where $r\ne0$. Find its gradient, then explain how it defines $F'(d)$.
examples.solution_text:
Rise: $F(d+r)-F(d)$.
Run: $(d+r)-d=r$.
$m_{\text{secant}}=\frac{F(d+r)-F(d)}{r}$.
As $r$ approaches zero, the secant gradient approaches the tangent gradient, provided the limit exists as a finite value.
$F'(d)=\lim_{r\to0}\frac{F(d+r)-F(d)}{r}$.

examples.derivation: The derivative equals the tangent gradient: (3−9)/(4−1)=−6/3=−2. This follows the supplied tangent-gradient teaching.

The tangent is y=x−1, containing P(3,2) and Q(5,4), so its gradient is (4−2)/(5−3)=1. The curve satisfies f(3+u)=2+u+0.4u²; its difference quotient at 3 is 1+0.4u, tending to 1. Thus the plotted line is the tangent at P and f′(3)=1.
A secant gradient measures average change between two distinct points. The tangent gradient at a gives the instantaneous rate f′(a), matching the supplied summary.
The vertical change is F(d+r)−F(d), and the horizontal change is (d+r)−d=r. Their quotient is the secant gradient; its finite limit as r→0 defines F′(d), as taught in the source investigation.
